turns.user: Daniel fell off a ladder at home and fractured his tibia. It's a closed fracture. What would his accident cover pay?
turns.visible:
If the Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee” (the row the document labels “Other Fracture”; these documents print no definition of which fractures that is), the conditional illustration is S$300,000: 50% of Daniel's sum insured of S$600,000 (Group Personal Accident), under the Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.
If the Simple Fracture benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee”, the conditional illustration is S$2,500: 50% of the Simple Fracture benefit limit of S$5,000, under the Group Insurance Product Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.
The accident wording says the benefit applies when bodily injury resulting from an accident causes a listed simple or other fracture.
Daniel’s Group Personal Accident amount is listed as S$600,000 as of 1 April 2024, which does not establish his cover on the accident date.
The Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary (page 8) prints “Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident” as a percentage of Daniel's own sum insured; the Group Insurance Product Summary (page 13) prints “Simple Fracture” as a percentage of a fixed Simple Fracture Benefit Limit. Neither document says whether one amends, replaces or adds to the other, or which applies to this event, so these are alternatives from separate documents, never a total.
Contact Aldermoor Life Ltd (through the employer or scheme administrator, for this group scheme) about the Scheme X Group Insurance - Certificate to ask what it needs for a claim.

turns.user: Daniel fell off a ladder at home and fractured his tibia. It's a closed fracture. What would his accident cover pay?
turns.visible:
If the Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee” (the row the document labels “Other Fracture”; these documents print no definition of which fractures that is), the conditional illustration is S$300,000: 50% of Daniel's sum insured of S$600,000 (Group Personal Accident), under the Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.
If the Simple Fracture benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee”, the conditional illustration is S$2,500: 50% of the Simple Fracture benefit limit of S$5,000, under the Group Insurance Product Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.
The accident wording says the benefit applies when bodily injury resulting from an Accident causes a listed fracture.
The Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary (page 8) prints “Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident” as a percentage of Daniel's own sum insured; the Group Insurance Product Summary (page 13) prints “Simple Fracture” as a percentage of a fixed Simple Fracture Benefit Limit. Neither document says whether one amends, replaces or adds to the other, or which applies to this event, so these are alternatives from separate documents, never a total.
Contact Aldermoor Life Ltd (through the employer or scheme administrator, for this group scheme) about the Scheme X Group Insurance - Certificate to ask what it needs for a claim.

details: If the Simple Fracture benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee”, the conditional illustration is S$2,500: 50% of the Simple Fracture benefit limit of S$5,000, under the Group Insurance Product Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.
The accident wording says the benefit applies when bodily injury resulting from an Accident causes a listed fracture.

The Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary (page 8) prints “Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident” as a percentage of Daniel's own sum insured; the Group Insurance Product Summary (page 13) prints “Simple Fracture” as a percentage of a fixed Simple Fracture Benefit Limit. Neither document says whether one amends, replaces or adds to the other, or which applies to this event, so these are alternatives from separate documents, never a total.
answer.summary: If the Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee” (the row the document labels “Other Fracture”; these documents print no definition of which fractures that is), the conditional illustration is S$300,000: 50% of Daniel's sum insured of S$600,000 (Group Personal Accident), under the Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.

passage.text:
G. Ambulance Cost
If an Insured Person sustains bodily injury as a result of an Accident, which necessitates the use of an ambulance, we will reimburse the actual
ground ambulance costs on a per event per Insured Person basis, incurred by the Insured Person up to maximum of $500 for transportation
(including the medical supplies used) to the Hospital.
This Benefit can only be claimed either under the Core Scheme or Voluntary Scheme.

Section 5 - Compassionate Death Allowance Benefit
If an Insured Person dies as a result of an Accident, we will pay the funeral expenses incurred, up to $2,000,
on receipt of proof of death and the relevant documents in our prescribed form.
This Benefit can only be claimed either under the Core Scheme or the Voluntary Scheme.

conversations.title: structured: Simple versus Other Fracture comparison

turns.user: Can you compare what the Simple Fracture benefit and the Other Fracture benefit would pay if Daniel broke his leg?
turns.visible:
If the Simple Fracture benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee”, the conditional illustration is S$2,500: 50% of the Simple Fracture benefit limit of S$5,000, under the Group Insurance Product Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.
If the Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee” (the row the document labels “Other Fracture”; these documents print no definition of which fractures that is), the conditional illustration is S$300,000: 50% of Daniel's sum insured of S$600,000 (Group Personal Accident), under the Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.
The Other Fracture wording applies to bodily injury resulting from an accident.
The Simple Fracture wording also requires bodily injury resulting from an accident.
The uploaded documents do not establish that both benefits can be claimed together, so these illustrations should not be added.
The Group Insurance Product Summary (page 13) prints “Simple Fracture” as a percentage of a fixed Simple Fracture Benefit Limit; the Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary (page 8) prints “Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident” as a percentage of Daniel's own sum insured. Neither document says whether one amends, replaces or adds to the other, or which applies to this event, so these are alternatives from separate documents, never a total.

turns.user: Can you compare what the Simple Fracture benefit and the Other Fracture benefit would pay if Daniel broke his leg?

details: If the Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident benefit applies to Daniel's case “Jaw, Pelvis, Leg, Ankle or Knee” (the row the document labels “Other Fracture”; these documents print no definition of which fractures that is), the conditional illustration is S$300,000: 50% of Daniel's sum insured of S$600,000 (Group Personal Accident), under the Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary; it is an illustration from the document's terms, not a payment or an insurer's decision.
The Other Fracture wording applies to bodily injury resulting from an accident.
The Simple Fracture wording also requires bodily injury resulting from an accident.
The uploaded documents do not establish that both benefits can be claimed together, so these illustrations should not be added.

The Group Insurance Product Summary (page 13) prints “Simple Fracture” as a percentage of a fixed Simple Fracture Benefit Limit; the Group Personal Accident Benefit Summary (page 8) prints “Simple Fracture or Other Fracture due to Accident” as a percentage of Daniel's own sum insured. Neither document says whether one amends, replaces or adds to the other, or which applies to this event, so these are alternatives from separate documents, never a total.
